chunks: And it has been narrated in another report:

Musa عليه السلام passed through Ṣafāʾiḥ al-Rawḥāʾ on a red camel, its bridle made of palm fiber, wearing two Qaṭawānī cloaks, and he was saying: ‘Labbayka, O Generous One, labbayk.’ And Yunus ibn Mattā عليه السلام passed through Ṣafāʾiḥ al-Rawḥāʾ while saying: ‘Labbayka, O Reliever of the tremendous distresses, labbayk.’ And ʿIsa ibn Maryam عليه السلام passed through Ṣafāʾiḥ al-Rawḥāʾ while saying: ‘Labbayka, Your servant, son of Your bondwoman, labbayk.’ And Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله passed through Ṣafāʾiḥ al-Rawḥāʾ while saying: ‘Labbayka, O Possessor of the Ascents, labbayk.’ And Musa عليه السلام used to recite the talbiyah, and the mountains would answer him. The talbiyah was named “response” because Musa عليه السلام responded to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and said: ‘Labbayk.’

key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةُ: The ritual proclamation of response to Allah recited in hajj.
key_terms.الرَّوْحَاءِ: Al-Rawḥāʾ, a place mentioned in the report through which the Prophets passed.
key_terms.ذَا الْمَعَارِجِ: An address to Allah meaning ‘Possessor of the Ascents.’
key_terms.عَبْدُكَ ابْنُ أَمَتِكَ: An expression of humility meaning ‘Your servant, son of Your bondwoman.’
key_terms.كَشَّافَ الْكُرَبِ الْعِظَامِ: An invocation meaning ‘Reliever of the tremendous distresses,’ used here in addressing Allah.
key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ: A declaration meaning ‘Here I am’ or ‘At Your service,’ expressing response and devotion to Allah.

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the talbiyah of the Prophets during hajj?
ai.summary: This report describes several Prophets عليهم السلام passing through al-Rawḥāʾ while proclaiming talbiyah, each invoking Allah with distinct words of devotion. It emphasizes the sacred history of hajj, the humility of the Prophets, and the meaning of talbiyah as a response to Allah, especially in the case of Musa عليه السلام.
